$comment: `risky` is the whole configuration decision. Everything else has a sane default.
Put a path here when a mistake in it reads as a plausible number instead of an error.
That is the test — not 'is it important'. A broken button is obvious the moment someone
looks. A permission check that silently passes, a total that is quietly 8,000 instead of
23,600, a status nothing handles — those look fine and stay wrong for months.
Keep the list short. A list that covers everything blocks every deploy, and a gate that
always blocks is a gate people learn to bypass.

risky.why: schema — a mistake here is not revertable by reverting
gut one and the suite still reports a pass
the guards themselves, and whatever decides if they run

$comment_verdict: The verdict lives in each review file as a marker — <!-- verdict: ship --> or
<!-- verdict: no-ship -->. It is not configured here and not parsed from prose, so there
is no language setting: the write-up may be in any language, only the marker is read.
No marker means the review does not count; if two disagree, no-ship wins.
$comment_tests: [name, command, why, options]. `optional: true` means missing prerequisites count as a
SKIP rather than a failure — and skips are named in the summary, every time. 'All green'
with two suites that never ran is a lie in a pleasant colour.
$comment_commands: Anything else that must pass. The exit code decides — never a string in the output.
